question: Does the 2020 Eagle Cement EIS provide usable Bulacan freshwater fish occurrence evidence, and is its fish paragraph independent of a similar 2022 Samar EIS paragraph?

primaryReport.citation: Eagle Cement Corporation. (2020). Environmental Impact Statement: Eagle Cement MPSA No. 245-2007-III Quarry Project. DENR-EMB EIA document repository.
projectLocationAsListed: Barangay Talbak, Doña Remedios Trinidad, Bulacan

pageLocators: printed page 152, section 2.2.3.4.4 Fish and other fauna
Table 19 caption for freshwater ecology component stations, San Ildefonso, November 2018

stationContext.fishStationLink: The EIS fish paragraph does not identify which, if any, of the four stations support each reported name. Do not carry station labels, coordinates, or reach labels onto the fish leads.

reportedFreshwaterContext.methodAsReported: The fish section says fish data came from chance interviews of residents and literature search. It does not identify which method supports each item and does not describe a fish capture, specimen, voucher, or fish-specific survey date.
reportedFreshwaterContext.reportedStatement: Locals reportedly named six fish and other aquatic animals that could be caught at sampling stations and said the forms were present in the river systems. This is a historical interview/literature statement, not verified capture evidence or current catchability.

textLineageScreen.observedSimilarity: The indexed 2022 Samar EIS repeats the same chance-interview/literature-search method wording and the same Biya/Gobiidae, Dalag/Channa sp., Hito/Clarias sp., shrimp, and small-crab labels. It reports five items and omits Eagle's tilapia item, whereas Eagle reports six.
textLineageScreen.interpretation: This near-verbatim cross-project wording is a report-template or source-lineage warning. The bounded text comparison cannot establish copying, shared interviewees, a shared underlying dataset, or independent observations. Do not treat the two reports as independent corroboration of any fish presence.
textLineageScreen.relationToSnmc: The Eagle EIS and 2023 SNMC EPRMP both name Conlong and Salapangan rivers in Bulacan, but differ in project/report and assessment context. Their overlapping locality names and interview/secondary-data methods do not establish independent fish evidence or a shared station-level dataset.

decision: Keep all six items as verbatim historical source-name leads only. The one species-rank label, Oreochromis niloticus, is not upgraded to a verified locality occurrence. No fish-to-station assignment or current-presence claim is supported.

rightsAndDisposition.itemSpecificReuseLicense: No item-specific open license or permission to redistribute report-derived fish information was verified.
rightsAndDisposition.contentHandling: No report PDF, page image, fish table, map, coordinates, interview record, photograph, or raw survey file was retained. Only concise source facts and source-name strings are recorded for internal research.

nextActions: Seek a lawfully accessible rendered EIS or underlying interview/literature citations to determine the source and evidence mode for each item; do not transcribe coordinates from the flattened Table 19 text without visual verification.

Compare citations and source acknowledgements in the Eagle and Samar reports before making any dataset-independence claim; the matching paragraph alone is insufficient to infer copying or independent confirmation.
Prioritize Bulacan sources that document fish collection, specimen or voucher identifiers, and a taxon-to-waterbody or station table over additional generic EIS interview lists.
